newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU's Kinnock says truck row violence inexcusable.
newsitem.headline: EU's Kinnock says truck row violence inexcusable.

text.p: European Transport Commissioner Neil Kinnock condemned on Friday outbreaks of violence in the escalating strike by Spanish truckers, urging Madrid to protect drivers from harm.
"I remain particularly concerned about the acts of violence that have been reported to me," Kinnock said in a statement.
"There is never any excuse for that in any industrial dispute and I have urged my Spanish colleague to take every possible measure to protect the security of Community hauliers," Kinnock said.
The Commissioner said his staff were in close contact with Spanish authorities to try to find a solution.
Spain's government was on Friday considering a demand that it reduce diesel prices in an attempt to curtail the burgeoning costs caused by the nine-day-old strike by truckers.
Striking truckers have choked roads in northern Spain, cut off supplies to many areas and forced factories to shut.
They want the retirement age lowered to 60 years from 65 and are pushing for diesel subsidies, a revision of tariffs and recognition of occupational illnesses.

Thousands of trucks lined the hard shoulders of main roads and pickets intimidated any drivers who dared to pass. They also blockaded border crossings, trapping hundreds of foreign drivers at the frontier.
More than a thousand Portuguese trucks were stranded at the border at Vilar Formoso and Caia, and hundreds of French trucks were also stuck at Behovia-Irun, local media said.
French truckers said Spanish pickets had attacked them.
British supermarket chain Tesco said its trucks were also damaged and a driver was sent to hospital after pickets dropped concrete from a motorway bridge.
Portugal's Ford, Volkswagen and AutoEuropa car manufacturers ordered special flights, while Tesco said it would fly food into Britain.
